attack_chain.action: The code tampers with the Exodus application by replacing its app.asar file and injecting a malicious webhook, bypassing security policies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Expanded data theft from Exodus users

attack_chain.action: A secondary payload is downloaded and executed; system defenses are disabled via PowerShell, security sites are blocked via hosts file modification, and malware files are hidden or deleted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence, evasion, and anti-forensics

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into Discord, and the process is forcibly restarted to ensure the payload is loaded and executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Hijacking of Discord sessions and further data theft

attack_chain.action: Stolen data is archived with password protection and exfiltrated via multiple channels, including file-sharing services and the Telegram bot API.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives and accesses the exfiltrated data

behavioral_signatures: Clipboard monitoring and replacement of cryptocurrency addresses using regex and pyperclip
Bulk access and theft of browser credentials, application data, and user files
Silent screenshot and webcam capture without user notification or consent
Tampering with third-party application files (e.g., Exodus app.asar, Discord application files)
Execution of PowerShell scripts to disable security tools and modify system settings
Modification of Windows hosts file to block access to security and antivirus domains
Creation and exfiltration of password-protected archives via multiple channels (file-sharing services, Telegram bot API)
file_indicators: Obfuscated or encrypted code present in __init__.py or main script files
Randomly named .pyw files appearing in temporary or user directories
Modified app.asar file in the Exodus application directory
Password-protected archive files (e.g., .zip, .rar) in temp or user folders
network_indicators: Outbound connections to hxxps://transfer[.]sh, gofile.io, anonfiles.com
Connections to Telegram bot API endpoints
Connections to bananasquad[.]ru, kekwltd[.]ru, paste.bingner[.]com
Outbound HTTP(S) requests to Discord webhook URLs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for clipboard access and replacement patterns matching cryptocurrency addresses, bulk file and credential access, unauthorized screenshot and webcam capture, and modification of third-party application files such as Exodus app.asar or Discord files. Detect execution of PowerShell scripts that disable security tools or modify the hosts file to block security domains. Flag packages containing obfuscated or encrypted code in __init__.py or main scripts, and monitor for outbound connections to known exfiltration and C2 domains (e.g., transfer.sh, gofile.io, Telegram bot API, Discord webhooks). Automated detection should correlate these behaviors and file/network indicators to identify malicious packages.
